brief: Cut my interview ~/Videos/i.mp4 down to 90 seconds, no ums, captions, 9:16.
requirements: The cut is made from the human's interview file ~/Videos/i.mp4 and nothing else: its real footage only, referenced read-only (path + sha256)
9:16 vertical deliverable (exact geometry): the footage is reframed so the speaker stays in frame and inside the safe area
'No ums': filler words (um, uh, you know) are removed - the removal is driven by the transcript, not guesswork - and verified: an ASR round trip on the final finds no fillers
Captions: word-accurate burned-in captions plus SRT from the same transcript, in the interview's language (English unless the audio says otherwise)
The 90 s is reached by cutting (selecting the best 90 seconds of the interview), not by speeding the footage or audio up
The piece contains only real footage from i.mp4 (no stock, no synthetic inserts - an edit cannot invent footage)
The clip reads as one coherent interview excerpt: clean in/out points, no mid-word cuts
Dialog audio stays clear: one mix at the loudness target (dialog bus, LUFS within 1, true peak <= -1 dBTP)
The human's file is never modified, moved or deleted (work happens on a conformed copy)
must_not: must not invent or substitute the interview (no stock footage, no synthetic stand-in, no similar file - the missing input is flagged, never faked)
must not pick a technique that cannot cut real footage (motion and math cannot edit the human's interview)
must not ignore 'no ums' (a plain duration trim that leaves fillers in fails the ask)
must not skip captions (an explicit ask)
must not deliver 16:9 or blind-crop the speaker out of frame (the ask is 9:16)
must not modify, move or delete the human's file
must not hit 90 s by speeding the footage up (a cut is a selection)
